summary.name: Alerting on SLOs like Pros
summary.one_liner: A SoundCloud engineering blog post describing how they implemented multiwindow, multi-burn-rate SLO alerts in Prometheus using HAProxy 5xx error rates.
use_cases: Setting up paging alerts that fire when an error budget burns quickly
Reducing on-call alert noise by alerting on user-facing symptoms
Configuring per-backend SLO error rate thresholds in Prometheus
Routing alerts to owning teams via Alertmanager labels
Creating ticket-level alerts for slow error budget burn
summary.what_it_does: The post explains how SoundCloud implemented SLO-based alerting using the error rate seen at its HAProxy edge layer, measured via the Prometheus HAProxy exporter. It sets a per-backend SLO error target through PromQL recording rules and computes 5xx error ratios over windows from 5m to 3d. Four multiwindow, multi-burn-rate alerts combine a long and short window with burn rate factors: two page-level alerts and two ticket-level alerts. The author also covers symptom vs. cause alerting, the use of a for clause to filter statistical outliers, and routing alerts to owning teams via a system label.
notable: Four alerts pairing long and short windows with burn rate factors (14.4, 6, 3, 1) to page on fast burn and ticket on slow burn
Per-backend SLO targets configured as PromQL recording rules
Uses a for clause despite the SRE Workbook advising against it, to guard against cold-start error spikes
Routes alerts to owning on-call teams via a system label generated from a team registry
caveats: Describes SoundCloud's internal setup; the exact alert rules are examples tailored to their HAProxy metrics and conventions
Relies on Prometheus and HAProxy exporter; HAProxy versions used were not yet natively instrumented for Prometheus at the time
